\subsection{Squarefree certificates and prime-primary linear rigidity}
\label{sec:linear-collision-rigidity}

The total degree of a critical Mahler certificate can have logarithmic
growth because multiplicities accumulate along power orbits.  The number of
distinct zeros and poles has a sharper bound.  For a reduced normalized
rational function
\[
 R=\frac AB,
 \qquad (A,B)=1,
 \qquad A(0)=B(0)=1,
\]
put
\[
 \rho(R):=\deg\rad(AB).
\]
Thus \(\rho(R)\) is the number of distinct non-zero zeros and poles over
\(\overline{\QQ}\), without multiplicity.

\begin{theorem}[Sharp squarefree Mahler bound]
\label{thm:squarefree-mahler-bound}
Let \(p\ge2\), and suppose that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:squarefree-mahler-coboundary}
 H(z)=\frac{P_0(z)}{P_1(z)}
 =\frac{R(z^p)}{R(z)^p},
\end{equation}
where \(P_0,P_1\in\QQ[z]\) are coprime,
\(P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1\), and \(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) satisfies \(R(0)=1\).
If
\[
 D=\deg P_0+\deg P_1,
\]
then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sharp-squarefree-mahler-bound}
 2(p-1)\rho(R)\le D.
\end{equation}
The constant \(2(p-1)\) is sharp for every \(p\ge2\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For \(\alpha\in\overline{\QQ}^{\times}\), write
\[
 e(\alpha)=\operatorname{ord}_{z=\alpha}H,
 \qquad
 r(\alpha)=\operatorname{ord}_{z=\alpha}R.
\]
Let \(S=\operatorname{supp}r\) and \(s=\abs S=\rho(R)\).  Since the input
in \eqref{eq:squarefree-mahler-coboundary} is reduced and has constant term
one,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:squarefree-input-l1-degree}
 D=\sum_{\alpha\in\overline{\QQ}^{\times}}\abs{e(\alpha)}.
\end{equation}
Taking divisors gives the identity already used in
\eqref{eq:p-mahler-divisor-recurrence}:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:squarefree-divisor-recurrence}
 e(\alpha)=r(\alpha^p)-p r(\alpha).
\end{equation}

For \(\beta\in S\), put
\[
 d_\beta=\#\{\alpha\in S:\alpha^p=\beta\}.
\]
Define a finitely supported function
\(\varphi:\overline{\QQ}^{\times}\to\{-1,0,1\}\) by
\[
 \varphi(\alpha)=
 \begin{cases}
  -\operatorname{sgn}r(\alpha),&\alpha\in S,\\
  \operatorname{sgn}r(\alpha^p),&\alpha\notin S,
       \ \alpha^p\in S,\\
  0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
Equations \eqref{eq:squarefree-input-l1-degree} and
\eqref{eq:squarefree-divisor-recurrence} imply
\begin{align}
 D
 &\ge \sum_\alpha e(\alpha)\varphi(\alpha)\notag\\
 &=\sum_{\beta\in S}r(\beta)
   \left(\sum_{\alpha^p=\beta}\varphi(\alpha)-p\varphi(\beta)\right).
 \label{eq:squarefree-dual-pairing}
\end{align}
Fix \(\beta\in S\).  Exactly \(p-d_\beta\) of its \(p\) distinct
\(p\)-th roots lie outside \(S\), and each contributes
\(\abs{r(\beta)}\) to the grouped summand in
\eqref{eq:squarefree-dual-pairing}.  Each of the \(d_\beta\) internal roots
contributes at least \(-\abs{r(\beta)}\), while
\[
 -p r(\beta)\varphi(\beta)=p\abs{r(\beta)}.
\]
The total contribution belonging to \(\beta\) is therefore at least
\(2(p-d_\beta)\abs{r(\beta)}\), and hence at least
\(2(p-d_\beta)\).  Consequently
\[
 D\ge2\sum_{\beta\in S}(p-d_\beta)
 =2\left(ps-\sum_{\beta\in S}d_\beta\right).
\]
Now
\[
 \sum_{\beta\in S}d_\beta
 =\#\{\alpha\in S:\alpha^p\in S\}\le s,
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:sharp-squarefree-mahler-bound}.

For sharpness, take \(R(z)=1-z^q\), where \(q\ge1\).  Then
\(\rho(R)=q\), and
\[
 \frac{R(z^p)}{R(z)^p}
 =\frac{1+z^q+\cdots+z^{(p-1)q}}{(1-z^q)^{p-1}}
\]
is reduced.  Its numerator and denominator both have degree
\((p-1)q\), so equality holds in
\eqref{eq:sharp-squarefree-mahler-bound}.
\end{proof}

The squarefree estimate controls collisions and a Taylor jet at the same
time.

\begin{theorem}[Collision--jet inequality]
\label{thm:collision-jet-inequality}
Under the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:squarefree-mahler-bound}, suppose in
addition that, for some \(x>0\),
\[
 R(t)>0\qquad(0\le t\le x),
\]
and that \(R\ne1\).  Put
\[
 \nu=\operatorname{ord}_{z=0}(R(z)-1),
 \qquad
 c_x(R)=\#\{y\in(0,x):R(y)=1\}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:collision-jet-bound}
 c_x(R)+\nu\le\rho(R)
 \le\left\lfloor\frac{D}{2(p-1)}\right\rfloor.
\end{equation}
Moreover
\[
 \operatorname{ord}_{z=0}(H(z)-1)=\nu.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The real function \(f(t)=\log R(t)\) has a zero of order \(\nu\) at zero.
If
\[
 0<y_1<\cdots<y_k<x
\]
are all its other zeros, then \(k=c_x(R)\).  The derivative
\(f'=R'/R\) has a zero of order at least \(\nu-1\) at zero, and Rolle's
theorem supplies a further zero in each of
\[
 (0,y_1),(y_1,y_2),\ldots,(y_{k-1},y_k).
\]
On the other hand, logarithmic differentiation gives
\[
 \frac{R'(z)}{R(z)}
 =\sum_{\alpha\in S}\frac{r(\alpha)}{z-\alpha}
 =\frac{N(z)}{\prod_{\alpha\in S}(z-\alpha)},
\]
where \(N\ne0\) and \(\deg N\le\abs S-1=\rho(R)-1\).  Counting the
zeros of \(N\), with multiplicity, yields
\[
 (\nu-1)+k\le\rho(R)-1.
\]
This proves the first inequality in \eqref{eq:collision-jet-bound}; the
second is \Cref{thm:squarefree-mahler-bound}.

Finally, if \(R(z)=1+az^\nu+O(z^{\nu+1})\), with \(a\ne0\), then
\[
 \frac{R(z^p)}{R(z)^p}=1-pa z^\nu+O(z^{\nu+1}),
\]
because \(p\nu>\nu\).  This proves the order identity.
\end{proof}

We now impose only a relative symmetry on a pair of extensions.  Let
\(\ell\) be prime, let \(G\) be a finite abelian \(\ell\)-group, and set
\[
 P_{\chi,\tau}(z)=\det(I-zA_{\chi,\tau}),
 \qquad
 H_\chi(z)=\frac{P_{\chi,\tau}(z)}{P_{\chi,\tau'}(z)}.
\]
The pair \((\tau,\tau')\) is \emph{relatively unit-Adams invariant} if
\begin{equation}\label{eq:relative-unit-adams}
 H_{\chi^u}(z)=H_\chi(z)
 \qquad
 (\chi\in\widehat G,\ (u,\ell)=1).
\end{equation}
This is weaker than requiring the two determinant families to be separately
unit-Adams invariant.

\begin{lemma}[Prime-primary Adams--M\"obius collapse]
\label{lem:prime-primary-adams-collapse}
Assume \eqref{eq:relative-unit-adams}, and put
\[
 \Delta_\chi(z)=F_\chi^\tau(z)-F_\chi^{\tau'}(z)
 =-\sum_{g\in G}\chi(g)
  \bigl(\mathcal E_g^\tau(z)-\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(z)\bigr).
\]
Then \(H_\chi\in\QQ(z)\), and on the common open Perron disk
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-adams-collapse}
 \Delta_\chi(z)
 =-\sum_{j\ge0}\ell^{-j}\Log_0H_\chi(z^{\ell^j})
  +\sum_{j\ge1}\ell^{-j}\Log_0H_{\chi^\ell}(z^{\ell^j}).
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The abelian form of \eqref{eq:fixed-determinant-open-disc} gives
\[

 succeeded in 283ms:

\begin{lemma}[Prime-primary Adams--M\"obius collapse]
\label{lem:prime-primary-adams-collapse}
Assume \eqref{eq:relative-unit-adams}, and put
\[
 \Delta_\chi(z)=F_\chi^\tau(z)-F_\chi^{\tau'}(z)
 =-\sum_{g\in G}\chi(g)
  \bigl(\mathcal E_g^\tau(z)-\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(z)\bigr).
\]
Then \(H_\chi\in\QQ(z)\), and on the common open Perron disk
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-adams-collapse}
 \Delta_\chi(z)
 =-\sum_{j\ge0}\ell^{-j}\Log_0H_\chi(z^{\ell^j})
  +\sum_{j\ge1}\ell^{-j}\Log_0H_{\chi^\ell}(z^{\ell^j}).
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The abelian form of \eqref{eq:fixed-determinant-open-disc} gives
\[
 \Delta_\chi(z)
 =-\sum_{k\ge1}\frac1k\sum_{d\mid k}\mu(d)
       \Log_0H_{\chi^d}(z^k).
\]
Write \(k=\ell^j q\), where \((q,\ell)=1\).  The squarefree divisors with
non-zero M\"obius value are \(d\mid q\), and, when \(j\ge1\), also
\(\ell d\).  Relative unit-Adams invariance gives
\[
 H_{\chi^d}=H_\chi,
 \qquad
 H_{\chi^{\ell d}}=H_{\chi^\ell}.
\]
The factor \(\sum_{d\mid q}\mu(d)\) vanishes unless \(q=1\), leaving
exactly \eqref{eq:prime-primary-adams-collapse}.

If \(K=\QQ(\chi(G))\), every element of \(\operatorname{Gal}(K/\QQ)\)
sends \(\chi\) to \(\chi^u\) for some \((u,\ell)=1\), and it sends
\(H_\chi\) to \(H_{\chi^u}\).  Thus \eqref{eq:relative-unit-adams} fixes
\(H_\chi\) under the full Galois group, proving
\(H_\chi\in\QQ(z)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Prime-primary collision--jet rigidity]
\label{thm:prime-primary-collision-jet-rigidity}
\label{thm:odd-adams-abelian-two-group-finite-sampling}
Let \(\ell\) be prime and let \(G\) be a finite abelian \(\ell\)-group.
Let \(\tau,\tau'\) be one-step \(G\)-cocycles over primitive non-negative
integral base matrices \(A,A'\), of sizes \(v,v'\), with Perron roots
\(\lambda,\lambda'>1\).  Put
\[
 x=\min\{\lambda^{-1},(\lambda')^{-1}\},
\]
and assume relative unit-Adams invariance
\eqref{eq:relative-unit-adams}.  Suppose that, for integers \(L\ge0\) and
\(K\ge1\),
\begin{align}
 p_{n,g}(\tau)&=p_{n,g}(\tau')
 &&(1\le n\le L,\ g\in G),
 \label{eq:prime-primary-initial-jet}\\
 \mathcal E_g^\tau(y_i)&=\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(y_i)
 &&(g\in G,\ 1\le i\le K),
 \label{eq:prime-primary-profile-samples}
\end{align}
at distinct radii \(0<y_i<x\), at least one of which is algebraic.  If
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-cross-base-threshold}
 K+L\ge\max\{v,v'\},
\end{equation}
then
\[
 p_{n,g}(\tau)=p_{n,g}(\tau')
 \qquad(n\ge1,\ g\in G).
\]
If the base determinants are already equal, it is enough to assume
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-fixed-determinant-threshold}
 K+L\ge
 \left\lfloor\frac{v+v'}{2(\ell-1)}\right\rfloor.
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Summing \eqref{eq:prime-primary-profile-samples} over \(g\) gives
\[
 \log\det(I-y_iA)=\log\det(I-y_iA')
 \qquad(1\le i\le K).
\]
Both determinants are positive on \((0,x)\), so their values agree at the
\(y_i\).  Likewise, summing \eqref{eq:prime-primary-initial-jet} over \(g\)
and using the primitive-orbit product gives
\[
 \det(I-zA)-\det(I-zA')=O(z^{L+1}).
\]
The polynomial on the left has degree at most \(\max\{v,v'\}\).  Under
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-cross-base-threshold}, its zero of multiplicity at
least \(L+1\) at zero and its \(K\) distinct positive zeros force it to
vanish identically.  Thus in either case under consideration the base
determinants agree and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-trivial-ratio}
 H_{\mathbf1}=1.
\end{equation}

Fourier transformation of \eqref{eq:prime-primary-profile-samples} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-fourier-samples}
 \Delta_\chi(y_i)=0
 \qquad(\chi\in\widehat G,\ 1\le i\le K).
\end{equation}
We prove \(H_\chi=1\) by induction on the order of \(\chi\).  The trivial
case is \eqref{eq:prime-primary-trivial-ratio}.  Let \(\chi\) have order
\(\ell^a\) and suppose that all lower-order character ratios are one.  Then
\(H_{\chi^\ell}=1\), and
\Cref{lem:prime-primary-adams-collapse} reduces to
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-one-orbit}
 \Delta_\chi(z)
 =-\sum_{j\ge0}\ell^{-j}\Log_0H_\chi(z^{\ell^j}).
\end{equation}

By \Cref{lem:prime-primary-adams-collapse}, \(H_\chi\in\QQ(z)\).  The
Perron-weighted domination in \Cref{lem:perron-weighted-domination} makes its
numerator and denominator zero-free on \(\abs z<x\).  Since
\(H_\chi(0)=1\) and \(H_\chi\) is real, it is positive on \((0,x)\).
Choose an algebraic sampled radius \(y_0\).  If \(H_\chi\ne1\), then
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-fourier-samples} and
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-one-orbit} give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-algebraic-product}
 \prod_{j\ge0}H_\chi(y_0^{\ell^j})^{\ell^{-j}}=1.
\end{equation}
Here all the hypotheses of
\Cref{thm:general-rational-p-mahler-lifting} apply to \(H_\chi\): it is
rational over \(\QQ\), one has \(0<y_0<x<1\), a radius
\(r\in(y_0,x)\) gives the required zero- and pole-free disk, and the
coefficient-height and common-denominator estimates are proved inside that
theorem for every rational input.  That theorem and
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-algebraic-product} therefore supply the unique
normalized \(R_\chi\in\QQ(z)^\times\) such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-rational-certificate}
 H_\chi(z)=\frac{R_\chi(z^\ell)}{R_\chi(z)^\ell},
 \qquad R_\chi(y_0)=1.
\end{equation}
The positive product defining the lift also shows that
\(R_\chi(t)>0\) for \(0\le t<x\).

Substitution of \eqref{eq:prime-primary-rational-certificate} into
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-one-orbit} telescopes to
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-rational-telescope}
 \Delta_\chi(z)=\ell\log R_\chi(z).
\end{equation}
Thus \eqref{eq:prime-primary-fourier-samples} gives
\(R_\chi(y_i)=1\) for every \(i\).  Moreover,
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-initial-jet} gives
\(\Delta_\chi(z)=O(z^{L+1})\), so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-certificate-jet}
 \nu_\chi:=\operatorname{ord}_{z=0}(R_\chi(z)-1)\ge L+1.
\end{equation}

Write \(H_\chi=P_{0,\chi}/P_{1,\chi}\) in reduced form and put
\(D_\chi=\deg P_{0,\chi}+\deg P_{1,\chi}\).  Cancellation from the two
original determinants can only lower degrees, hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-input-degree}
 D_\chi\le v+v'.
\end{equation}
Applying \Cref{thm:collision-jet-inequality} to
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-rational-certificate} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-final-count}
 K+L+1\le K+\nu_\chi
 \le\rho(R_\chi)
 \le\left\lfloor\frac{D_\chi}{2(\ell-1)}\right\rfloor.
\end{equation}
The last member is at most \(\max\{v,v'\}\), contradicting
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-cross-base-threshold}; when the base determinants were
known in advance, \eqref{eq:prime-primary-input-degree} instead makes
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-final-count} contradict
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-fixed-determinant-threshold}.  Therefore
\(H_\chi=1\), closing the induction.

All character determinants now agree.  The comparison dictionary in
\Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary}, followed by Fourier inversion on \(G\),
recovers every primitive length--element count.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Linear radial determination]
\label{cor:prime-primary-linear-radial-determination}
Under the hypotheses of
\Cref{thm:prime-primary-collision-jet-rigidity}, with \(L=0\),
\(\max\{v,v'\}\) full profile vectors, one algebraically anchored, determine
all primitive length--element data.  In particular, \(V\) radial locations
suffice for bases of size at most \(V\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Exact order of binary radial sampling complexity]
\label{cor:exact-binary-radial-sampling-order}
For \(V\ge6\), the universal binary radial determination number from
\Cref{cor:linear-radial-sampling-lower-bound} satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-binary-radial-sampling-order}
 \left\lfloor\frac{V-2}{4}\right\rfloor+1
 \le\mathsf N_{C_2}(V)\le V.
\end{equation}
Consequently \(\mathsf N_{C_2}(V)=\Theta(V)\), which closes the sampling
complexity order exactly.
\end{corollary}

\subsection{Odd-prime multi-collisions with delayed discrepancy}
\label{sec:odd-prime-delayed-multicollisions}

The prime-primary theorem has realizable odd-prime examples with linearly
many collisions and a delayed first discrepancy.

\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

For relatively unit-Adams-invariant extensions by any finite abelian
\(\ell\)-group \(G\), with \(\ell\) prime, over two primitive bases of at
most \(V\) vertices, \(V\) radial locations in the common open Perron
interval determine the complete primitive length--element profile, provided
that one location is algebraic.  More generally, \(K\) radial profiles and
agreement of the first \(L\) primitive vectors suffice when
\(K+L\ge\max\{v,v'\}\).  This radial depth is independent of the rank and
exponent of \(G\), while each location supplies a full
\(\abs G\)-component vector.  The bases need not coincide.  A
strict twisted gap permits centered, not raw, class profiles at a Perron
endpoint in the binary scalar theorem.  The determinant ratio governing the
test is canonically the ratio of the standard Artin--Mazur zeta functions of
the two binary covers.  The proof is effective: one algebraic collision
produces a unique rational Mahler certificate.  Its squarefree degree satisfies
\(2(p-1)\deg\rad(AB)\le D\), and the collision--jet inequality converts this
directly into the linear radial theorem.  For every fixed \(p\ge2\), the
separate total-degree estimate bounds the numerator-plus-denominator degree
of this multiplicative certificate, from the reduced input degree alone, by
\(b_p(D)=O_p(D\log D)\).  Its order is sharp abstractly and on realizable
standard \(C_2\)-cover zeta ratios.  The explicit height and fixed-\(p\) bit
complexity estimates are useful further consequences; the finite Pad\'e
system is rational reconstruction under the resulting cap.  The exact four-vertex
pair shows why a single centered Perron-boundary vector cannot be an inverse
invariant; every corresponding raw class profile diverges to \(-\infty\).
For every \(m\), an explicit binary pair on a common \(4m+2\)-vertex positive
base has \(m\) distinct rational collisions but different periodic data.
For each odd prime \(\ell\), a pair on \(\ell(2m+1)\) vertices has \(m\)
rational collisions, agrees through length \(m\), and first differs at length
\(m+1\) by an explicit element vector.
The logarithmic certificate-degree order is also sharp on standard realizable
\(C_2\)-cover zeta ratios.

The determinant lifting theorem is a specialization of a parity-free rational
critical \(p\)-Mahler statement.  Its coefficient recursion gives the exact
bound
\[
 (pq)^{2n-1}f_n\in\ZZ,\qquad
 \log d_h\le(2h-1)\log(pq),
\]
which is sufficient for Kumiko Nishioka's 1982 special-value theorem.
The cited algebraic-solution rationality result of Keiji Nishioka from 1985
then makes the algebraic solution rational, and normalization over \(\QQ\)
supplies the coboundary.  Determinant parity is therefore a convenient strong
sufficient condition yielding integral coefficients through
Dieudonn\'e--Dwork, not an essential lifting hypothesis.  The endpoint form
still uses the strict gap only to continue through the Perron circle.

The full prime-primary Adams--M\"obius collapse is written explicitly, and
induction on character order reduces each relatively unit-Adams-invariant
channel to one \(\ell\)-Mahler orbit.  The same mechanism does not presently
yield a polynomial sample
bound for every finite group.  For \(C_3\), Adams--M\"obius inversion already couples
two character determinants at infinitely many arithmetically distributed
powers, rather than one lacunary Mahler orbit.  A general finite-group theorem
therefore requires a new special-value and effective zero theory for these
coupled Euler systems.  Generic \(C_4\) outside the relative unit-Adams-invariant
subclass has the analogous coupled obstruction.  In its absence, the proved
general statement remains unconditional analytic recovery from a profile set
with an interior accumulation point.

The novelty claim is correspondingly narrow.  The parity-free lifting theorem
is explicitly a combination of the two Nishioka inputs and the elementary
denominator estimate, rather than a new special-value theory.
Frobenius-class Euler products, their character expansion,
algebraic-solution rationality for rational functional equations, and the
general periodic-data dictionary are cited background.  The original Mahler
increment is the input-only \(b_p(D)\) divisor estimate for the multiplicative
certificate, its \(\Omega_p(D\log D)\) family, and the transfer of that
sharpness to realizable \(C_2\)-cover zeta ratios.  The height bound and fixed-
\(p\) integer bit complexity are useful but incremental.  Bare existence and
decidability reduce, by logarithmic differentiation, to the published
additive and linear Mahler algorithms; Pad\'e reconstruction is largely
standard after a degree cap is known.  The central result is instead the
cross-base prime-primary linear inverse theorem, together with the realizable
binary and odd-prime multi-collision families.

The principal dynamical theorem remains an inverse theorem for the
paper-specific sampled fixed-label Euler values.  Its standard dynamical
conclusion is represented periodic-data equivalence, via the cited
determinant/periodic-data dictionary.  It does not advance conjugacy, strong
shift equivalence, cocycle cohomology, switching, Bowen--Franks or flow
equivalence, or full positivity realization.  The structural reasons are
that class counts discard marked-orbit holonomy, determinant data discard
positive matrix factorization, the relative realization lemma chooses a
large common base only after the candidate polynomials are fixed, and the
arithmetic reduction controls a scalar \(p\)-power orbit rather than the
coupled character systems required beyond the stated class.

inversion expresses every \(F_\phi\) through the finite determinant family,
but it does so at all powers \(z^k\).  Finite radial determination is therefore
a special-value problem, not a coefficient-counting consequence of the
determinant degrees.

\subsection{Main results}

We first state the squarefree estimate that drives the linear theorem.  For
\(p\ge2\), reduce
\[
 H(z)=\frac{P_0(z)}{P_1(z)}=\frac{R(z^p)}{R(z)^p},
 \qquad R=\frac AB,
\]
with both fractions normalized and reduced, and put
\(D=\deg P_0+\deg P_1\).  \Cref{thm:squarefree-mahler-bound} proves
\begin{equation}\label{eq:intro-collision-bound}
 2(p-1)\deg\rad(AB)\le D.
\end{equation}
If \(R\) is positive on a real interval, then
\Cref{thm:collision-jet-inequality} strengthens this to
\[
 \#\{y:R(y)=1\}+\operatorname{ord}_0(R-1)
 \le\deg\rad(AB)\le\left\lfloor\frac{D}{2(p-1)}\right\rfloor.
\]
The estimate counts distinct singularities, so repeated multiplicities along
long power orbits do not introduce the logarithmic factor present in the
total certificate degree.

The proof has two independent parts.  First,
\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} shows that one algebraic interior
collision, without a spectral gap, or one endpoint collision under the gap,
forces the exact rational Mahler coboundary
\[
 H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2},\qquad R(0)=R(y)=1.
\]
The general lifting theorem does not require determinant parity.  Its
coefficient recursion gives the explicit bound
\((pq)^{2n-1}f_n\in\ZZ\), hence \(\log d_h=O(h)\) for the common
denominators; Kumiko Nishioka's special-value theorem then forces algebraicity,
and the cited 1985 result of Keiji Nishioka gives rationality.  We verify every
hypothesis of Kumiko Nishioka's printed theorem, including the critical
inequality \(p^2<p^3\).  Parity and Dieudonn\'e--Dwork remain available only
as a stronger integrality refinement.  Separately,
\Cref{prop:logarithmic-mahler-divisor-bound} proves the paper's
total-degree Mahler estimate: the reduced input degree \(D\) alone bounds
\(\deg A+\deg B\) for the multiplicative certificate \(R=A/B\) by
\(b_p(D)=O_p(D\log D)\).  This is not a bound for an additive
logarithmic-derivative certificate or for an arbitrary rational solution of a
general linear Mahler equation.  The \(\Omega_p(D\log D)\) family makes the
order sharp, and \Cref{cor:realizable-logarithmic-certificate-sharpness}
transports that sharpness to standard realizable \(C_2\)-cover zeta ratios.
The supporting \Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} also records
an explicit height estimate and fixed-base bit complexity, while its finite
Pad\'e step implements rational reconstruction once a degree cap is known.
The collision radii are exactly the positive zeros of \(R-1\).

The principal inverse theorem is not confined to a common base, to one binary
coordinate, or to the prime two.  Let \(\ell\) be prime, let \(G\) be a finite
abelian \(\ell\)-group, and suppose that the pair of cocycles satisfies
\[
 \frac{P_{\chi^u,\tau}(z)}{P_{\chi^u,\tau'}(z)}
 =\frac{P_{\chi,\tau}(z)}{P_{\chi,\tau'}(z)}
 \qquad(\chi\in\widehat G,\ (u,\ell)=1).
\]
By \Cref{thm:prime-primary-collision-jet-rigidity}, \(K\) common profile
vectors, with one algebraic anchor, together with agreement of the first
\(L\) primitive vectors determine all primitive length--element counts when
\(K+L\ge\max\{v,v'\}\).  In particular, \(V\) radial locations suffice for
bases of at most \(V\) vertices.  Summing the element profiles first recovers
the base determinant.  The prime-primary Adams--M\"obius collapse is
\[
 \Delta_\chi(z)
 =-\sum_{j\ge0}\ell^{-j}\log H_\chi(z^{\ell^j})
  +\sum_{j\ge1}\ell^{-j}\log H_{\chi^\ell}(z^{\ell^j}).
\]
Induction on the order of \(\chi\) applies the scalar lifting and the
collision--jet inequality.  One observation at a radius means the entire
\(G\)-valued vector \((\mathcal E_g(y))_{g\in G}\), so the radial depth is
independent of the rank and exponent of \(G\).  For \(C_2\) the relative
symmetry is automatic.

One centered radius cannot suffice.  \Cref{thm:c2-boundary-collision} gives
two strict-gap labellings of the same four-vertex graph with different
length-one class counts but identical centered class Euler profiles at the
Perron radius.  Their raw class profiles both diverge there.  The centered
identity is exact and comes from
\(Q(z^2)/Q(z)^2\), where \(Q(z)=1-z+4z^2\) and \(Q(1/4)=1\).

The realizable lower bound grows linearly.
\Cref{thm:realizable-linear-multicollisions} constructs, for every \(m\ge1\),
two strict-gap cocycles on the same positive \(4m+2\)-vertex base with
different periodic data and equality of both element profiles at \(m\)
distinct rational radii.  Hence
\[
 \mathsf N_{C_2}(V)\ge
 \left\lfloor\frac{V-2}{4}\right\rfloor+1.
\]
For odd primes, \Cref{thm:odd-prime-delayed-multicollisions} constructs two
unit-Adams-invariant \(C_\ell\)-cocycles on a common
\(\ell(2m+1)\)-vertex positive base.  Their full profiles agree at \(m\)
rational radii, their primitive data agree through length \(m\), and their
first discrepancy at length \(m+1\) is explicit.  Separately,
\Cref{cor:realizable-logarithmic-certificate-sharpness} realizes the abstract
\(\Omega(D\log D)\) certificate-degree family on standard covers.

For an arbitrary finite group, \Cref{thm:radial-profile-recovery} proves,
again without a twisted-gap hypothesis, recovery from a set with an interior
accumulation point.  We do not claim a
finite polynomial sample bound in that generality.  The precise obstruction
to extending the present method is recorded after
\Cref{thm:finite-radial-sampling}: already for \(C_3\), the
Adams--M\"obius coefficient is non-zero at infinitely many prime powers and
does not reduce to a one-variable Mahler orbit.  The missing input is a
special-value and effective zero theorem for that coupled cyclotomic Euler
system.  The same obstruction remains for generic \(C_3\)- and
\(C_4\)-cocycles outside the relative unit-Adams condition.  Thus the
prime-primary theorem identifies the symmetric subclass handled by the
one-variable method; it does not assert an unrestricted finite-group theorem.

\subsection{Prior work and scope}

The Frobenius-class objects used here have a direct dynamical lineage.
Parry--Pollicott prove a Chebotarev asymptotic for primitive closed orbits in a
prescribed Frobenius conjugacy class in finite Galois covers of Axiom~A flows,
and Noorani--Parry prove the finite homogeneous-extension analogue for shifts
\cite{ParryPollicott1986Chebotarev,NooraniParry1992ChebotarevShifts}.
Mohamed--Noorani then prove a class-restricted Mertens product for finite-group
extensions of SFTs: their Theorem~1 has the product
\[
 \prod_{\substack{|\gamma|\le N\\g_\gamma\in C}}
 (1-e^{-h|\gamma|})
\]
with exponent \(|C|/|G|\) and a constant expressed through Artin
\(L\)-values \cite[Theorem~1, pp.~124--125]
{MeslizaNoorani1999FrobeniusMertens}.  Noorani's later toral paper instead
classifies the lift-degree partitions of closed orbits in a finite torsion
cover and gives asymptotic counts for each realizable partition
\cite{Noorani2003ClosedOrbitsToral}.  These are orbit-distribution and product
results, not finite-special-value inverse theorems.

the fixed base gives equality of the scalar coordinate, while
\(\mathbf1_{\{e\}}=(\mathbf1+\varepsilon)/2\) and
\(\mathbf1_{\{s\}}=(\mathbf1-\varepsilon)/2\).  Therefore equality of
\(\Delta_\varepsilon(y)\) is equivalent to
\(\mathcal D_{\{e\}}(y)=\mathcal D_{\{s\}}(y)=0\), proving the last
assertion.

If both sign blocks have strict spectral radius below \(\lambda\), their
determinants are zero-free on a disk strictly larger than \(\abs z\le x\).
The identity \eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}, the lifting theorem,
and the rational telescoping formula then hold also at \(x\).  Since the base
is common, the class-profile differences equal the differences of the centered
profiles.  This gives precisely the asserted centered endpoint extension.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Linear radial locations for elementary two-groups]
\label{thm:elementary-two-group-finite-sampling}
Let \(E=(C_2)^r\), with \(r\ge0\).  Let
\(\tau:E(\Gamma)\to E\) and \(\tau':E(\Gamma')\to E\) be one-step
cocycles over primitive non-negative integral base matrices \(A,A'\), whose
sizes are at most \(V\) and whose Perron roots \(\lambda,\lambda'>1\) need
not agree.  Put
\[
 x=\min\{\lambda^{-1},(\lambda')^{-1}\},
 \qquad M(V)=V.
\]
For \(g\in E\), define
\[
 \mathcal E_g^\tau(y)=\sum_{n\ge1}p_{n,g}(\tau)\log(1-y^n),
 \qquad 0<y<x,
\]
and define \(\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}\) analogously.  Suppose that
\[
 \mathcal E_g^\tau(y_i)=\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(y_i)
 \qquad(g\in E,\ 1\le i\le M(V))
\]
at \(M(V)\) distinct radii in \((0,x)\), at least one of which is
algebraic.  Then
\[
 p_{n,g}(\tau)=p_{n,g}(\tau')
 \qquad(n\ge1,\ g\in E).
\]
One radial observation here means the full vector
\((\mathcal E_g(y_i))_{g\in E}\).  Thus the theorem uses \(M(V)\)
radial locations independently of \(r\), while the total number of scalar
equalities assumed is \(|E|M(V)=2^rM(V)\).  Neither a common base
presentation nor a strict spectral gap for the non-trivial character blocks
is required.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Absolute convergence follows for each system from the periodic-point estimate
used in \Cref{thm:finite-radial-sampling}.  Summing the assumed identities over
\(g\in E\) gives, at every sampled radius,
\[
 \log\det(I-y_iA)=\sum_{g\in E}\mathcal E_g^\tau(y_i)
 =\sum_{g\in E}\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(y_i)
 =\log\det(I-y_iA').
\]
Both determinants are positive on \((0,x)\).  Their difference has degree at
most \(V\), vanishes at the \(M(V)\ge V\) distinct non-zero sample points,
and also vanishes at zero.  Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:elementary-two-group-base-determinant-equality}
 \det(I-zA)=\det(I-zA').
\end{equation}

Every \(\chi\in\widehat E\) takes values in \(\{\pm1\}\).  Let
\(B_{\chi,\tau}\) and \(B_{\chi,\tau'}\) be the corresponding character
blocks and put
\[
 H_\chi(z)=\frac{\det(I-zB_{\chi,\tau})}
                  {\det(I-zB_{\chi,\tau'})}.
\]
Since \(\chi(g)\equiv1\pmod2\), entrywise reduction gives
\[
 B_{\chi,\tau}\equiv A\pmod2,
 \qquad B_{\chi,\tau'}\equiv A'\pmod2.
\]
Together with \eqref{eq:elementary-two-group-base-determinant-equality}, this
shows that the two character determinants are congruent modulo two and hence
supports the integral refinement in
\Cref{lem:critical-mahler-integrality}; the two blocks need not have the same
size.  This congruence is not an input to the parity-free lifting theorem
\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} used below.

Fourier transformation of the sampled class-profile identities gives
\[
 \Delta_\chi(y_i):=
 \sum_{g\in E}\chi(g)
 \bigl(\mathcal E_g^\tau(y_i)-\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(y_i)\bigr)=0.
\]
For the trivial character this is already
\eqref{eq:elementary-two-group-base-determinant-equality}.  For non-trivial
\(\chi\), one has \(\chi^m=\chi\) for odd \(m\) and
\(\chi^m=\mathbf1\) for even \(m\).  The Adams--M\"obius calculation in
\eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}, with the now common trivial
determinant coordinate, therefore gives
\[
 \Delta_\chi(y)=\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H_\chi(y^{2^j}).
\]

Choose an algebraic sampled radius \(y_0\).  If \(H_\chi\ne1\),
\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} supplies the unique normalized
\(R_\chi\in\QQ(z)^\times\) such that
\[
 H_\chi(z)=\frac{R_\chi(z^2)}{R_\chi(z)^2},
 \qquad R_\chi(y_0)=1.
\]
Write the reduced ratio \(H_\chi=P_{0,\chi}/P_{1,\chi}\) and put
\(D_\chi=\deg P_{0,\chi}+\deg P_{1,\chi}\).  Both character determinants
have degree at most \(V\), so \(D_\chi\le2V\).  The positive telescoping
identity in \Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} shows that all real zeros
of \(\Delta_\chi\) lie among the positive roots of \(R_\chi-1\).  Since
\(R_\chi(0)=1\), \(R_\chi\ne1\), and \(R_\chi\) is positive on the common
Perron interval, \Cref{thm:collision-jet-inequality} gives at most
\[
 \left\lfloor\frac{D_\chi}{2}\right\rfloor-1
 \le V-1=M(V)-1
\].
The \(M(V)\) sampled zeros are therefore impossible.  Thus \(H_\chi=1\)
for every character \(\chi\).  The cross-base periodic-data dictionary in
\Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary}, followed by character Fourier inversion,
now gives equality of every primitive length--element count.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Located obstruction for general finite groups]
\label{rem:general-group-finite-sampling-interface}
For a same-base pair and \(\pi\in\Irr(G)\), put
\(H_\pi=P_{\pi,\tau}/P_{\pi,\tau'}\); then \(H_{\mathbf1}=1\).
Rearranging \eqref{eq:fixed-determinant-open-disc} by \(k=rm\) gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:general-group-adams-mobius-obstruction}
 \begin{aligned}
 F_{\chi_\rho}^\tau(z)-F_{\chi_\rho}^{\tau'}(z)
   &=-\sum_{k\ge1}\frac1k\sum_{\pi\in\Irr(G)}
       b_{\rho,\pi}(k)\Log_0H_\pi(z^k),\\
 b_{\rho,\pi}(k)
   &=\sum_{m\mid k}\mu(m)a_{\rho,\pi}^{(m)}.
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
For \(C_2\), projection away from the common trivial channel makes these
coefficients vanish unless \(k\) is a power of two.  That lacunarity is exactly

sufficient condition for a general abelian \(2\)-group is that, for every
ordered vertex pair, every \(g\in G\), and every odd \(u\), the number of
\(g\)-labelled edges equals the number of \(g^u\)-labelled edges.  It then
gives \(A_{\chi^u}=A_\chi\), not merely equality of their determinants.

For \(C_4=\langle a\rangle\), this condition says exactly that the
\(a\)- and \(a^{-1}\)-labelled edge counts agree entrywise; the \(e\)- and
\(a^2\)-counts are unrestricted.  It does not force factorization through
\(C_2\): a one-vertex graph with equally many \(a\)- and \(a^{-1}\)-loops
has primitive base and holonomy subgroup \(C_4\).  Likewise, assigning equal
counts on each odd-power orbit in \(C_{2^s}\) gives examples with genuine
holonomy of order \(2^s\).
\end{remark}

odd-prime constructions are unconditional.  Subject to the explicitly
quoted assumption \textup{(KN85)}, they also give the stronger linear
prime-primary theorem and the upper bound \(\mathsf N_{C_2}(V)\le V\).

The determinant lifting theorem is a specialization of a parity-free rational
critical \(p\)-Mahler statement.  Its coefficient recursion gives the exact
bound
\[
 (pq)^{2n-1}f_n\in\ZZ,\qquad
 \log d_h\le(2h-1)\log(pq),
\]
which is sufficient for Kumiko Nishioka's 1982 special-value theorem.
The cited algebraic-solution rationality result of Keiji Nishioka from 1985
then makes the algebraic solution rational, and normalization over \(\QQ\)
supplies the coboundary.  Determinant parity is therefore a convenient strong
sufficient condition yielding integral coefficients through
Dieudonn\'e--Dwork, not an essential lifting hypothesis.  The endpoint form
still uses the strict gap only to continue through the Perron circle.

The full prime-primary Adams--M\"obius collapse is written explicitly, and
induction on character order reduces each relatively unit-Adams-invariant
channel to one \(\ell\)-Mahler orbit.  The same mechanism does not presently
yield a polynomial sample
bound for every finite group.  For \(C_3\), Adams--M\"obius inversion already couples
two character determinants at infinitely many arithmetically distributed
powers, rather than one lacunary Mahler orbit.  A general finite-group theorem
therefore requires a new special-value and effective zero theory for these
coupled Euler systems.  Generic \(C_4\) outside the relative unit-Adams-invariant
subclass has the analogous coupled obstruction.  In its absence, the proved
general statement remains unconditional analytic recovery from a profile set
with an interior accumulation point.

The novelty claim is correspondingly narrow.  The parity-free lifting theorem
is explicitly a combination of the two Nishioka inputs and the elementary
denominator estimate, rather than a new special-value theory.
Frobenius-class Euler products, their character expansion,
algebraic-solution rationality for rational functional equations, and the
general periodic-data dictionary are cited background.  The original Mahler
increment is the input-only \(b_p(D)\) divisor estimate for the multiplicative
certificate, its \(\Omega_p(D\log D)\) family, and the transfer of that
sharpness to realizable \(C_2\)-cover zeta ratios.  The height bound and fixed-
\(p\) integer bit complexity are useful but incremental.  Bare existence and
decidability reduce, by logarithmic differentiation, to the published
additive and linear Mahler algorithms; Pad\'e reconstruction is largely
standard after a degree cap is known.  The central result is instead the
cross-base prime-primary linear inverse theorem, together with the realizable
binary and odd-prime multi-collision families.

The principal dynamical theorem remains an inverse theorem for the
paper-specific sampled fixed-label Euler values.  Its standard dynamical
conclusion is represented periodic-data equivalence, via the cited
determinant/periodic-data dictionary.  It does not advance conjugacy, strong
shift equivalence, cocycle cohomology, switching, Bowen--Franks or flow
equivalence, or full positivity realization.  The structural reasons are
that class counts discard marked-orbit holonomy, determinant data discard
positive matrix factorization, the relative realization lemma chooses a
large common base only after the candidate polynomials are fixed, and the
arithmetic reduction controls a scalar \(p\)-power orbit rather than the
coupled character systems required beyond the stated class.

Kumiko Nishioka's Theorem~5.1.7 is the standard reference for the linear
Mahler rational--transcendental dichotomy: it applies to \(k\)-Mahler
functions defined by a linear functional equation
\cite[Theorem~5.1.7]{Nishioka1996MahlerFunctions}; see also
\cite[Corollary~8]{BellCoonsRowland2013MahlerDichotomy}.  The equation
\(F(z^2)=H(z)^{-1}F(z)^2\) is quadratic in \(F\) and therefore lies outside
that class; Keiji Nishioka's nonlinear class
\(f(z^p)=\mathscr R(z,f(z))\) is the applicable result.

\begin{proposition}[Algebraic critical products are rational coboundaries]
\label{prop:algebraic-mahler-coboundary}
Let \(p\ge2\), let \(H\in\QQ(z)^\times\), \(H(0)=1\), and suppose that
\(F\in1+z\QQ[[z]]\) is algebraic over \(\CC(z)\) and satisfies
\(F(z)^p=H(z)F(z^p)\).  Then there is a unique
\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\), normalized by \(R(0)=1\), such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:general-rational-mahler-coboundary}
 H(z)=\frac{R(z^p)}{R(z)^p}.
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The cited 1985 algebraic-solution rationality result of Keiji Nishioka gives,
in the one-variable form used here, that an algebraic Laurent-series solution of
\(f(z^p)=\mathscr R(z,f(z))\), with \(\mathscr R\) rational, belongs to
\(\CC(z)\) \cite{Nishioka1985AlgebraicSolutions}.  Apply it with
\(\mathscr R(z,Y)=Y^p/H(z)\).  Thus \(F\in\CC(z)\).
Because the normalized Taylor germ of \(F\) has coefficients in \(\QQ\),
coefficientwise Galois invariance gives \(F\in\QQ(z)\).  Taking
\(R=F^{-1}\) in the displayed functional equation gives
\[
 H(z)=\frac{R(z^p)}{R(z)^p},\qquad R(0)=1.
\]
For uniqueness, if \(U(0)=1\) and \(U(z^p)=U(z)^p\), a least non-constant
term \(az^n\) would occur in degree \(pn\) on the left and degree \(n\) on
the right.  Hence \(U=1\).  The rationality implication used here is the cited
result of Keiji Nishioka; the only descent specific to the present
normalization is from the rational Taylor germ to \(\QQ(z)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[General rational critical \(p\)-Mahler lifting]
\label{thm:general-rational-p-mahler-lifting}
Let \(p\ge2\), let \(H\in\QQ(z)^\times\) satisfy \(H(0)=1\), and suppose
that \(H\) has neither a zero nor a pole on \(\abs z<r\).  On that disk define
the normalized analytic function
\begin{equation}\label{eq:general-critical-p-mahler-product}
 F_{H,p}(z):=\prod_{\nu\ge0}
 H(z^{p^\nu})^{p^{-\nu-1}},
 \qquad F_{H,p}(0)=1,
\end{equation}
using the logarithm germ at zero.  Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:general-critical-p-mahler-equation}
 F_{H,p}(z)^p=H(z)F_{H,p}(z^p).
\end{equation}
If \(\alpha\ne0\) is algebraic,

If \(\textup{(i)}\) holds, positivity and
\eqref{eq:critical-product-square-normalization} give \(F(y)=1\).
\Cref{thm:general-rational-p-mahler-lifting}, with \(p=2\), then gives the
unique normalized rational certificate and \(R(y)=1\).  This is
\(\textup{(ii)}\).  Conversely, \(\textup{(ii)}\) and
\eqref{eq:rational-mahler-telescope} give \(\textup{(i)}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Scope of the lifting theorem]
Determinant parity is a convenient sufficient condition for the integral
refinement in \Cref{lem:critical-mahler-integrality}, but it is not necessary
for special-value lifting.  The general result
\Cref{thm:general-rational-p-mahler-lifting} applies to every rational \(H\)
with the stated analytic orbit conditions; its arithmetic input is instead
the elementary denominator estimate
\[
 (pq)^{2n-1}f_n\in\ZZ,\qquad
 \log d_h\le(2h-1)\log(pq).
\]
Thus the lifting is, explicitly, the combination of Kumiko Nishioka's 1982
special-value theorem, the cited algebraic-solution rationality result of
Keiji Nishioka from 1985, and this coefficient estimate.  We retain
Dieudonn\'e--Dwork only for the stronger integral conclusion when parity is
available.  For example, the determinant-realizable subclass remains broad.
Fix \(r\ge2\), an odd \(a>0\), and a positive even \(b\), and let \(A\) have
diagonal entries \(a\) and off-diagonal entries \(b\).  Then
\(\lambda=a+(r-1)b\).  Any diagonal \(B=\operatorname{diag}(c_i)\) and
\(B'=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)\), with odd
\(\abs{c_i},\abs{d_i}\le a\), satisfies the same-base compatibility and
strict gaps, and realizes
\[
 H(z)=\frac{\prod_i(1-c_i z)}{\prod_i(1-d_i z)}.
\]
\end{remark}

## Current priority boundary (15 August 2026)

The current manuscript uses the following narrower priority narrative, which
supersedes any broader wording in earlier audit notes:

- Ostrowski (1968) treats the linear multiplicative equation
  `Phi(phi(z)) = g(z) Phi(z)` for rational data.
- Kumiko Nishioka, *Mahler Functions and Transcendence* (1996), Theorem 5.1.7,
  is the standard reference for the rational--transcendental dichotomy for
  `k`-Mahler functions defined by a linear functional equation. Bell, Coons and
  Rowland, arXiv:1210.2070v2, Corollary 8, gives an open-access restatement and
  a new proof.
- The equation `F(z^2) = H(z)^(-1) F(z)^2` is quadratic in `F` and therefore
  outside that linear class. Keiji Nishioka's 1985 nonlinear class
  `f(z^p) = R(z,f(z))` is the applicable result, with `p = 2` and
  `R(z,Y) = Y^2/H(z)`. This algebraic-to-rational step is prior work and is not
  a contribution of the paper.
- Springer keeps the cited 1985 pages 330--335 behind subscription, and
  Unpaywall reported no open-access copy; this audit does not record a
  first-hand check of the printed text.
- The paper's claimed Mahler contribution is limited to the input-only divisor
  estimate for the multiplicative certificate, its sharp lower-bound family
  and realizable transfer, and the supporting explicit height and fixed-base
  integer bit analysis. Bare existence and decidability are prior, and the
  Pade step is largely standard rational reconstruction after a degree cap is
  known. The tier-carrying claim is the cross-base odd-Adams-invariant
  abelian-two-group dynamical inverse theorem.

In particular, the paper does not claim originality for the general
algebraic-solution rationality theorem, for the fixed-label Euler coordinate,

# Finite radial determination for abelian two-group SFT extensions

This directory builds two related papers.

- `main.tex` is the inverse-theorem manuscript. Its spine is finite radial
  determination for odd-Adams-invariant extensions by arbitrary finite
  abelian 2-groups over possibly different bases, without a twisted-gap
  hypothesis in the open Perron interval. It also contains the parity-free
  rational critical Mahler lifting theorem, a sharp input-only divisor bound
  for its multiplicative certificate, and realizable lower-bound families on
  standard `C2` covers. Height and fixed-base bit bounds are recorded as
  supporting effective consequences.
- `supplement.tex` contains the Adams-corrected Frobenius-class product
  constant, quotient-cover refinements, and the exact strict-gap `S3`
  witness. These results are logically separate from the inverse theorem.

For base matrices of size at most `V`, the proved uniform sampling budget is

```text
M(V) = 2 V ceil(log2(4V)).
```

The radii lie in the common open Perron interval and at least one is
algebraic. A strict twisted gap is required only for the binary endpoint
extension. The theorem is automatic for elementary 2-groups and covers
genuine higher 2-power holonomy under odd-Adams invariance. A standard-cover
family gives an `Omega(V)` sampling lower bound, while a separate realizable
family shows that the `O(D log D)` Mahler certificate-degree bound has the
correct order.

No finite polynomial sampling bound is claimed for every finite group. The
paper locates the obstruction already at `C3`: Adams--Mobius inversion has
non-lacunary support and produces a coupled cyclotomic Euler system for which
the required special-value and effective zero theorems are not available.

Build and exact-verification commands are recorded in `REPRODUCE.md`.
Dear Editors,

We submit "Finite radial determination of Frobenius profiles for
odd-Adams-invariant abelian two-group extensions of shifts of finite type"
for consideration as a Research Article in Ergodic Theory and Dynamical
Systems.

The paper proves finite radial determination for odd-Adams-invariant
extensions by arbitrary finite abelian two-groups over primitive edge shifts,
allowing the two base shifts to be different. The number of radial locations
is independent of the group rank and exponent. The class contains every
elementary two-group extension and standard extensions with genuine holonomy
of order 4, 8, and beyond. The paper also gives an exact boundary collision, a
realizable linear sampling lower bound, and the obstruction to extending the
finite bound to arbitrary finite groups. Its arithmetic engine includes a
strong supporting Mahler theorem: an input-only O(D log D) divisor estimate
for the multiplicative certificate itself, a matching lower-bound family, and
transfer of that sharpness to standard realizable C2-cover zeta ratios.
Explicit height and fixed-base bit-complexity estimates complete the effective
treatment.

The priority claim is deliberately narrow. Ostrowski treats the linear
multiplicative equation. The cited algebraic-solution rationality result of
Keiji Nishioka from 1985 supplies rationality for the squared functional
equation used here. The parity-free lifting theorem is explicitly a
combination of Kumiko Nishioka's 1982 special-value theorem, that cited
rationality result, and an elementary denominator estimate, rather than a new
special-value theory. Bare existence and decidability of the rational
certificate are prior through published additive and linear Mahler algorithms,
and the finite Pade step is largely standard rational reconstruction once a
degree bound is known. The claimed Mahler increment is therefore the
input-only multiplicative-certificate bound, its sharpness, and the supporting
integer height and fixed-base bit analysis, not a new general Mahler decision
algorithm.

ETDS is the coherent home because the submission is led by the dynamical
inverse theorem and its realizable dynamical lower bounds, at an interface
with number theory and combinatorics. The Mahler component improves
completeness and effectivity rather than the journal-tier case. We considered
but declined splitting the paper: a symbolic-computation venue would not fit
the present whole, and the realizable C2-cover family gives the supporting
Mahler theorem its strongest meaning inside the unified dynamics paper.

The submission includes separately compiled Supplementary Material containing
the Frobenius-class product-constant companion results, quotient-cover

Title: Finite radial determination of Frobenius profiles for odd-Adams-invariant abelian two-group extensions of shifts of finite type

Authors:

## Abstract

Let G be a finite abelian 2-group, and assume that the twisted determinants
of two one-step G-cocycles are invariant under every odd Adams operation.
The cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts whose vertex counts are at most
V; the bases need not be the same. For the primitive length-element counts
p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1) p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap
hypothesis, equality of every element profile at
2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron interval forces
equality of every p_(n,g), provided that one sampled radius is algebraic.
The number of radial locations is independent of the rank and exponent of G.
The hypothesis is automatic for G=(C2)^r and permits genuine holonomy of
orders 4, 8, and beyond. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: a parity-free
rational critical p-Mahler lifting theorem combines an elementary
linear-exponent denominator estimate with Kumiko Nishioka's special-value
theorem and the cited algebraic-solution rationality result of Keiji
Nishioka. Determinant parity gives a stronger integral refinement but is not
needed for lifting. For the multiplicative certificate itself, an input-only
divisor estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound in terms of the reduced
input degree alone. Its order is sharp abstractly and on standard realizable
C2-cover zeta ratios. Explicit height and fixed-p bit bounds are supporting
quantitative consequences; the Pade step is rational reconstruction after a
degree cap is known. A second standard-cover family gives m exact rational collisions on
4m+2 vertices and hence an Omega(V) sampling lower bound. For general finite
groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation point;
already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a finite
bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

Keywords: one-sided edge shift; finite-group extension; inverse problem;
Mahler function; twisted determinant; Adams operation; primitive orbit;
finite sampling

2020 MSC: 37B10; 11B85; 39A06; 20C15; 05C25

Competing interests: The authors declare none.

## Venue and paper architecture

ETDS remains a defensible ambitious submission because the principal result
is the dynamical inverse theorem: finite radial determination of represented
periodic data for odd-Adams-invariant finite abelian two-group extensions,
with cross-base recovery, rank- and exponent-independent radial depth, exact
collisions, and realizable lower bounds. This is a central dynamical problem
at the interface with number theory and combinatorics. The Mahler theorem is a
strong supporting theorem that improves the paper's completeness and
effectivity; it does not carry the journal-tier case.

A symbolic-computation venue is not a better home for the present whole
paper, whose headline and standard conclusion are dynamical. A focused
functional-equations extraction was considered, but splitting was declined:
the quantitative Mahler result is more meaningful here because its sharpness
is realized by standard C2-cover zeta ratios, while the dynamics paper uses
the result as its effective arithmetic engine.

## Supplement policy

Checked 2026-08-15 against the ETDS "Preparing your materials" instructions:
https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/ergodic-theory-and-dynamical-systems/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials

The instructions expressly permit supplementary materials and state that they
are published online alongside the article. The supplement and reproducibility
archive may therefore remain separate; no content needs to be moved into the
main manuscript.

## Priority boundary

Ostrowski (1968) treats the linear multiplicative equation. The cited
algebraic-solution rationality result of Keiji Nishioka (1985) supplies the
rationality implication for `F(z^2)=H(z)^(-1)F(z)^2`; the submission makes no
originality claim for that implication. The parity-free lifting theorem is
explicitly the combination of Kumiko Nishioka's 1982 special-value theorem,
the cited Keiji Nishioka result, and an elementary denominator estimate. The
claimed contribution is limited to parity-compatible algebraic collision
lifting in the dynamical setting, the input-only multiplicative-certificate
divisor estimate and its sharp lower-bound family, the supporting height and
fixed-p bit estimates, the cross-base odd-Adams-invariant abelian 2-group
theorem, and the realizable certificate-degree and linear sampling lower
bounds. Bare existence and decidability are prior; once a degree bound is
known, the Pade step is largely standard rational reconstruction.

\title[Finite radial determination]{Finite radial determination of
Frobenius profiles for odd-Adams-invariant abelian two-group extensions of
shifts of finite type}

\author[Haobo Ma]{Haobo Ma}
\address{AELF PTE. LTD., \#14-02, Marina Bay Financial Centre Tower 1,
8 Marina Boulevard, Singapore 018981, Singapore}
\email{auric@aelf.io}
\author[Wenlin Zhang]{Wenlin Zhang}
\address{National University of Singapore, 21 Lower Kent Ridge Road,
Singapore 119077, Singapore}
\email{e1327962@u.nus.edu}
\thanks{Corresponding author: Wenlin Zhang.}
\date{}
\renewcommand{\shortauthors}{H. Ma and W. Zhang}

\begin{document}

\begin{abstract}
Let \(G\) be a finite abelian \(2\)-group, and assume that the twisted
determinants of two one-step \(G\)-cocycles are invariant under every odd
Adams operation \(\chi\mapsto\chi^u\).  The cocycles lie over primitive edge
shifts whose vertex counts are at most \(V\); the bases need not be the same.
For the primitive length--element counts \(p_{n,g}\), put
\(\mathcal E_g(y)=\sum_{n\ge1}p_{n,g}\log(1-y^n)\).  Without a twisted-gap
hypothesis, equality of every element profile at
\[
 2V\lceil\log_2(4V)\rceil
\]
distinct radii in the common open Perron interval forces equality of every
\(p_{n,g}\), provided that one sampled radius is algebraic.  Thus the number
of radial locations is independent of the rank and exponent of \(G\), although
each location supplies the full \(\abs G\)-component profile vector.  The
hypothesis is automatic for \(G=(C_2)^r\) and permits genuine holonomy of
orders \(4,8,\ldots\).  For a reduced binary character-determinant ratio of
total degree \(D>0\), one algebraic collision identifies the complete real
collision set, which has at most
\(D\lceil\log_2(2D)\rceil-1\) points.

The sign-determinant ratio is canonically the ratio of the ordinary
Artin--Mazur zeta functions of the two \(C_2\)-covers.  The inverse mechanism
is arithmetic: a single algebraic interior collision forces this ratio to be
a normalized rational Mahler coboundary
\(R(z^2)/R(z)^2\).  More generally, a rational critical \(p\)-Mahler product
with one algebraic value is algebraic by an elementary linear-exponent
denominator estimate and Kumiko Nishioka's critical special-value theorem.
The algebraic-to-rational implication attributed to Keiji Nishioka is used in
the explicitly stated assumption \textup{(KN85)} for the conditional linear
prime-primary result; its bibliographic record, but not its original printed
statement, has been verified.  Determinant parity and the
Dieudonn\'e--Dwork criterion give a stronger integral refinement but are not
needed for lifting.  For the multiplicative certificate \(R=A/B\), a new
squarefree divisor estimate gives
\[
 2(p-1)\deg\rad(AB)\le D.
\]
Together with Rolle's theorem, it bounds the number of positive collisions
plus the first non-zero Taylor order of \(R-1\).  A separate divisor
\(\ell_1\) estimate gives the input-only total-degree bound
\(\deg A+\deg B\le b_p(D)=O_p(D\log D)\) in terms of the reduced input degree
\(D\).  An \(\Omega_p(D\log D)\) family makes this order sharp, and the same
order occurs for standard realizable \(C_2\)-cover zeta ratios.  Explicit
height control and fixed-\(p\) polynomial bit complexity are further
quantitative consequences; once the degree cap is known, the displayed
Pad\'e step is rational reconstruction.  Conditional on \textup{(KN85)}, the
squarefree estimate gives a linear prime-primary collision--jet theorem.
An exact four-vertex pair shows that one centered
Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice; the uncentered class profiles
diverge there.  More generally, the binary construction on a common
\(4m+2\)-vertex positive base gives \(m\) rational collisions, while for
every odd prime \(\ell\) a pair on \(\ell(2m+1)\) vertices has \(m\) rational
collisions, agrees through length \(m\), and first differs explicitly at
length \(m+1\).  A companion-matrix realization transfers the
\(\Omega(D\log D)\) certificate-degree family to standard zeta ratios.  For general finite
groups we prove
recovery from a radial set with an interior accumulation point and identify
the obstruction to a finite bound: already for \(C_3\), Adams--M\"obius
inversion couples determinant logarithms at infinitely many arithmetically
distributed powers, outside the one-variable Mahler theorem used here.
\end{abstract}

Mahler function, twisted determinant, Adams operation, primitive orbit,

 succeeded in 281ms:
If \(K=\QQ(\chi(G))\), every element of \(\operatorname{Gal}(K/\QQ)\)
sends \(\chi\) to \(\chi^u\) for some \((u,\ell)=1\), and it sends
\(H_\chi\) to \(H_{\chi^u}\).  Thus \eqref{eq:relative-unit-adams} fixes
\(H_\chi\) under the full Galois group, proving
\(H_\chi\in\QQ(z)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional prime-primary collision--jet rigidity]
\label{thm:prime-primary-collision-jet-rigidity}
Let \(\ell\) be prime and let \(G\) be a finite abelian \(\ell\)-group.
Let \(\tau,\tau'\) be one-step \(G\)-cocycles over primitive non-negative
integral base matrices \(A,A'\), of sizes \(v,v'\), with Perron roots
\(\lambda,\lambda'>1\).  Put
\[
 x=\min\{\lambda^{-1},(\lambda')^{-1}\},
\]
and assume relative unit-Adams invariance
\eqref{eq:relative-unit-adams}.  Suppose that, for integers \(L\ge0\) and
\(K\ge1\),
\begin{align}
 p_{n,g}(\tau)&=p_{n,g}(\tau')
 &&(1\le n\le L,\ g\in G),
 \label{eq:prime-primary-initial-jet}\\
 \mathcal E_g^\tau(y_i)&=\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(y_i)
 &&(g\in G,\ 1\le i\le K),
 \label{eq:prime-primary-profile-samples}
\end{align}
at distinct radii \(0<y_i<x\), at least one of which is algebraic.  If
the following statement, denoted \textup{(KN85)}, holds:
\begin{quote}
For every integer \(p\ge2\) and every \(H\in\CC(z)^\times\), every
convergent Laurent-series germ \(F\in\CC((z))\) that is algebraic over
\(\CC(z)\) and satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:kn85-explicit-assumption}
 F(z^p)=\frac{F(z)^p}{H(z)}
\end{equation}
belongs to \(\CC(z)\),
\end{quote}
then, if
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-cross-base-threshold}
 K+L\ge\max\{v,v'\},
\end{equation}
then
\[
 p_{n,g}(\tau)=p_{n,g}(\tau')
 \qquad(n\ge1,\ g\in G).
\]
If the base determinants are already equal, it is enough to assume
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-fixed-determinant-threshold}
 K+L\ge
 \left\lfloor\frac{v+v'}{2(\ell-1)}\right\rfloor.
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Summing \eqref{eq:prime-primary-profile-samples} over \(g\) gives
\[
 \log\det(I-y_iA)=\log\det(I-y_iA')
 \qquad(1\le i\le K).
\]
Both determinants are positive on \((0,x)\), so their values agree at the
\(y_i\).  Likewise, summing \eqref{eq:prime-primary-initial-jet} over \(g\)
and using the primitive-orbit product gives
\[
 \det(I-zA)-\det(I-zA')=O(z^{L+1}).
\]
The polynomial on the left has degree at most \(\max\{v,v'\}\).  Under
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-cross-base-threshold}, its zero of multiplicity at
least \(L+1\) at zero and its \(K\) distinct positive zeros force it to
vanish identically.  Thus in either case under consideration the base
determinants agree and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-trivial-ratio}
 H_{\mathbf1}=1.
\end{equation}

Fourier transformation of \eqref{eq:prime-primary-profile-samples} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-fourier-samples}
 \Delta_\chi(y_i)=0
 \qquad(\chi\in\widehat G,\ 1\le i\le K).
\end{equation}
We prove \(H_\chi=1\) by induction on the order of \(\chi\).  The trivial
case is \eqref{eq:prime-primary-trivial-ratio}.  Let \(\chi\) have order
\(\ell^a\) and suppose that all lower-order character ratios are one.  Then
\(H_{\chi^\ell}=1\), and
\Cref{lem:prime-primary-adams-collapse} reduces to
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-one-orbit}
 \Delta_\chi(z)
 =-\sum_{j\ge0}\ell^{-j}\Log_0H_\chi(z^{\ell^j}).
\end{equation}

By \Cref{lem:prime-primary-adams-collapse}, \(H_\chi\in\QQ(z)\).  The
Perron-weighted domination in \Cref{lem:perron-weighted-domination} makes its
numerator and denominator zero-free on \(\abs z<x\).  Since
\(H_\chi(0)=1\) and \(H_\chi\) is real, it is positive on \((0,x)\).
Choose an algebraic sampled radius \(y_0\).  If \(H_\chi\ne1\), then
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-fourier-samples} and
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-one-orbit} give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-algebraic-product}
 \prod_{j\ge0}H_\chi(y_0^{\ell^j})^{\ell^{-j}}=1.
\end{equation}
Define the convergent germ
\[
 F_\chi(z)=\prod_{j\ge0}H_\chi(z^{\ell^j})^{\ell^{-j}}.
\]
It belongs to \(1+z\QQ[[z]]\) and satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-critical-equation}
 F_\chi(z^\ell)=\frac{F_\chi(z)^\ell}{H_\chi(z)}.
\end{equation}
The proof of \Cref{thm:general-rational-p-mahler-lifting}, through its
application of Kumiko Nishioka's 1982 theorem, applies verbatim: one has
\(0<y_0<x<1\), a radius \(r\in(y_0,x)\) gives the required zero- and
pole-free disk, and that proof establishes the coefficient-height and
common-denominator bounds for every rational input.  Hence
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-algebraic-product}, which says \(F_\chi(y_0)=1\),
forces \(F_\chi\) to be algebraic over \(\CC(z)\).  Assumption
\textup{(KN85)} applied to \eqref{eq:prime-primary-critical-equation} now
gives \(F_\chi\in\CC(z)\).  Since its Taylor coefficients are rational,
coefficientwise Galois invariance gives \(F_\chi\in\QQ(z)\).  Therefore
\(R_\chi=F_\chi^{-1}\) is the unique normalized element of
\(\QQ(z)^\times\) such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-rational-certificate}
 H_\chi(z)=\frac{R_\chi(z^\ell)}{R_\chi(z)^\ell},
 \qquad R_\chi(y_0)=1.
\end{equation}
The positive product defining the lift also shows that
\(R_\chi(t)>0\) for \(0\le t<x\).

Substitution of \eqref{eq:prime-primary-rational-certificate} into
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-one-orbit} telescopes to
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-rational-telescope}
 \Delta_\chi(z)=\ell\log R_\chi(z).
\end{equation}
Thus \eqref{eq:prime-primary-fourier-samples} gives
\(R_\chi(y_i)=1\) for every \(i\).  Moreover,
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-initial-jet} gives
\(\Delta_\chi(z)=O(z^{L+1})\), so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-certificate-jet}
 \nu_\chi:=\operatorname{ord}_{z=0}(R_\chi(z)-1)\ge L+1.
\end{equation}

Write \(H_\chi=P_{0,\chi}/P_{1,\chi}\) in reduced form and put
\(D_\chi=\deg P_{0,\chi}+\deg P_{1,\chi}\).  Cancellation from the two
original determinants can only lower degrees, hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-input-degree}
 D_\chi\le v+v'.
\end{equation}
Applying \Cref{thm:collision-jet-inequality} to
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-rational-certificate} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-final-count}
 K+L+1\le K+\nu_\chi
 \le\rho(R_\chi)
 \le\left\lfloor\frac{D_\chi}{2(\ell-1)}\right\rfloor.
\end{equation}
The last member is at most \(\max\{v,v'\}\), contradicting
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-cross-base-threshold}; when the base determinants were
known in advance, \eqref{eq:prime-primary-input-degree} instead makes
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-final-count} contradict
\eqref{eq:prime-primary-fixed-determinant-threshold}.  Therefore
\(H_\chi=1\), closing the induction.

All character determinants now agree.  The comparison dictionary in
\Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary}, followed by Fourier inversion on \(G\),
recovers every primitive length--element count.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Conditional linear radial determination]
\label{cor:prime-primary-linear-radial-determination}
Assume \textup{(KN85)}: for every \(p\ge2\) and
\(H\in\CC(z)^\times\), every convergent Laurent-series germ
\(F\in\CC((z))\) algebraic over \(\CC(z)\) and satisfying
\(F(z^p)=F(z)^p/H(z)\) belongs to \(\CC(z)\).  Under the remaining
hypotheses of \Cref{thm:prime-primary-collision-jet-rigidity}, with \(L=0\),
\(\max\{v,v'\}\) full profile vectors, one algebraically anchored, determine
all primitive length--element data.  In particular, \(V\) radial locations
suffice for bases of size at most \(V\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Conditional binary linear sampling bound]
\label{cor:exact-binary-radial-sampling-order}
Assume \textup{(KN85)}: for every \(p\ge2\) and
\(H\in\CC(z)^\times\), every convergent Laurent-series germ
\(F\in\CC((z))\) algebraic over \(\CC(z)\) and satisfying
\(F(z^p)=F(z)^p/H(z)\) belongs to \(\CC(z)\).  Then, for \(V\ge6\),
the universal binary radial determination number from
\Cref{cor:linear-radial-sampling-lower-bound} satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-binary-radial-sampling-order}
 \left\lfloor\frac{V-2}{4}\right\rfloor+1
 \le\mathsf N_{C_2}(V)\le V.
\end{equation}
Thus \textup{(KN85)} would imply
\(\mathsf N_{C_2}(V)=\Theta(V)\).  Unconditionally, the displayed lower
bound remains valid.
\end{corollary}

\subsection{Odd-prime multi-collisions with delayed discrepancy}
\label{sec:odd-prime-delayed-multicollisions}

The following unconditional construction gives odd-prime examples with
linearly many collisions and a delayed first discrepancy.

\begin{theorem}[Odd-prime multi-collisions with delayed first discrepancy]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the artifact tests and archive a timing-free LF transcript."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path


MODULES = (
    "artifacts.test_verify_a5_results",
    "artifacts.test_verify_linear_collision_claims",
    "artifacts.test_verify_twisted_determinant_rigidity",
)


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output",
        type=Path,
        default=Path(__file__).with_name("unittest_output.txt"),
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()
    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    display_command = "python -m unittest -v " + " ".join(MODULES)
    command = [sys.executable, "-m", "unittest", "-v", *MODULES]
    completed = subprocess.run(
        command,
        cwd=root,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
    )
    transcript = completed.stdout + completed.stderr
    print(transcript, end="")
    stable_transcript = re.sub(
        r"^(Ran \d+ tests?) in [0-9.]+s$",
        r"\1",
        transcript.replace("\r\n", "\n"),
        flags=re.MULTILINE,
    )
    archive = (
        f"Python version: {sys.version.split()[0]}\n"
        f"command: {display_command}\n"
        "random seed: none (deterministic)\n\n"
        + stable_transcript
    )
    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.output.write_text(archive, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    return completed.returncode


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

FINITE RADIAL DETERMINATION OF FROBENIUS PROFILES FOR ODD-ADAMS-INVARIANT ABELIAN TWO-GROUP EXTENSIONS OF SHIFTS OF FINITE TYPE
HAOBO MA AND WENLIN ZHANG 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification. 37B10, 11B85, 39A06, 20C15, 05C25. Key words and phrases. One-sided edge shift, finite-group extension, inverse problem, Mahler function, twisted determinant, Adams operation, primitive orbit, finite sampling. Corresponding author: Wenlin Zhang.
1

2
Abstract. Let G be a finite abelian 2-group, and assume that the twisted determinants of two one-step G-cocycles are invariant under every odd Adams operation   u. The cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts whose vertex counts are at most V ; the bases need not be the same. For the primitive length�element counts pn,g, put Eg(y) = n1 pn,g log(1-yn). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every element profile at
2V log2(4V )
distinct radii in the common open Perron interval forces equality of every pn,g, provided that one sampled radius is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of the rank and exponent of G, although each location supplies the full |G|-component profile vector. The hypothesis is automatic for G = (C2)r and permits genuine holonomy of orders 4, 8, . . .. For a reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D > 0, one algebraic collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most D log2(2D) - 1 points.
The sign-determinant ratio is canonically the ratio of the ordinary Artin�Mazur zeta functions of the two C2-covers. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: a single algebraic interior collision forces this ratio to be a normalized rational Mahler coboundary R(z2)/R(z)2. More generally, a rational critical p-Mahler product with one algebraic value is algebraic by an elementary linear-exponent denominator estimate and Kumiko Nishioka's critical special-value theorem. The algebraic-to-rational implication attributed to Keiji Nishioka is used in the explicitly stated assumption (KN85) for the conditional linear prime-primary result; its bibliographic record, but not its original printed statement, has been verified. Determinant parity and the Dieudonn�Dwork criterion give a stronger integral refinement but are not needed for lifting. For the multiplicative certificate R = A/B, a new squarefree divisor estimate gives
2(p - 1) deg rad(AB)  D.
Together with Rolle's theorem, it bounds the number of positive collisions plus the first non-zero Taylor order of R - 1. A separate divisor 1 estimate gives the input-only total-degree bound deg A + deg B  bp(D) = Op(D log D) in terms of the reduced input degree D. An p(D log D) family makes this order sharp, and the same order occurs for standard realizable C2-cover zeta ratios. Explicit height control and fixed-p polynomial bit complexity are further quantitative consequences; once the degree cap is known, the displayed Pad� step is rational reconstruction. Conditional on (KN85), the squarefree estimate gives a linear prime-primary collision�jet theorem. An exact four-vertex pair shows that one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice; the uncentered class profiles diverge there. More generally, the binary construction on a common 4m + 2-vertex positive base gives m rational collisions, while for every odd prime  a pair on (2m + 1) vertices has m rational collisions, agrees through length m, and first differs explicitly at length m + 1. A companion-matrix realization transfers the (D log D) certificate-degree family to standard zeta ratios. For general finite groups we prove recovery from a radial set with an interior accumulation point and identify the obstruction to a finite bound: already for C3, Adams�M�bius inversion couples determinant logarithms at infinitely many arithmetically distributed powers, outside the one-variable Mahler theorem used here.

None of the five results depends on Kumiko Nishioka 1982 alone. Theorem 5.1 is the only primary result that uses Kumiko 1982, and it subsequently requires the Keiji 1985 interface.

**Hypothesis Boundary**

For Theorem 2.1, the required hypotheses are \(p\ge2\), normalized reduced fractions
\[
H=\frac{P_0}{P_1}=\frac{R(z^p)}{R(z)^p},\qquad
P_0(0)=P_1(0)=R(0)=1,
\]
with \(P_0,P_1\in\mathbb Q[z]\), \(R\in\mathbb Q(z)^\times\), and \(D=\deg P_0+\deg P_1\). These are internal hypotheses; no external theorem is used.

Theorem 3.1 adds \(R\ne1\), positivity \(R(t)>0\) on the stated real interval, and the definitions
\[
\nu=\operatorname{ord}_0(R-1),\qquad
c_x(R)=\#\{y\in(0,x):R(y)=1\}.
\]
Again, all inputs are internal.

Theorem 5.1 requires:

- \(\ell\) prime and \(G\) a finite abelian \(\ell\)-group.
- Primitive nonnegative integral base matrices \(A,A'\), with the stated Perron interval.
- Relative unit-Adams invariance.
- Agreement of the first \(L\) primitive length-element vectors.
- \(K\) distinct interior profile collisions, one at an algebraic radius.
- The applicable threshold on \(K+L\).
- The explicitly quoted assumption `(KN85)`.

Everything except `(KN85)` and the published Kumiko special-value theorem is established internally. Corollary 5.3 inherits these hypotheses in the binary specialization and separately requires \(V\ge6\).

Theorem 6.1 assumes only an odd prime \(\ell\ge3\) and \(m\ge1\); its systems are constructed explicitly.

**The Descent Step**

The descent to the relative ratio \(H_\chi\) itself is valid:

- Relative unit-Adams invariance genuinely gives \(H_\chi\in\mathbb Q(z)\).
- Perron domination supplies the required zero- and pole-free disk.
- The algebraic sample lies inside that disk, so its full power orbit avoids zeros and poles.
- The coefficient-height and common-denominator estimates required by Kumiko Nishioka 1982 are established for this rational input.
- The checked Kumiko theorem therefore implies that
  \[
  F_\chi(z)=\prod_{j\ge0}H_\chi(z^{\ell^j})^{\ell^{-j}}
  \]
  is algebraic over \(\mathbb C(z)\).

That is exactly where the proof stops using verified inputs. Kumiko 1982 alone does not produce \(F_\chi\in\mathbb C(z)\), so it does not produce the rational certificate \(R_\chi=F_\chi^{-1}\). Without that certificate, the squarefree collision-jet inequality cannot be applied and character induction does not close.

The exact Keiji 1985 statement required to close the proof mechanically is now quoted in the theorem hypothesis:

> For every integer \(p\ge2\) and every \(H\in\mathbb C(z)^\times\), every convergent Laurent-series germ \(F\in\mathbb C((z))\) that is algebraic over \(\mathbb C(z)\) and satisfies
> \[
> F(z^p)=\frac{F(z)^p}{H(z)}
> \]
> belongs to \(\mathbb C(z)\).

Once this implication is verified from the original paper, the remaining descent is elementary: rational Taylor coefficients give \(F\in\mathbb Q(z)\) by coefficientwise Galois invariance, and \(R=F^{-1}\) gives
\[
H(z)=\frac{R(z^p)}{R(z)^p}.
\]

The pre-certificate portion of Theorem 5.1 is salvageable with Kumiko 1982 alone: base-determinant recovery, the prime-primary Adams-Möbius collapse, rationality and zero-freedom of \(H_\chi\), the algebraic collision identity, and algebraicity of \(F_\chi\). The rigidity conclusion and linear upper bound are not.

| Theorem 5.1, prime-primary collision-jet rigidity | Kumiko Nishioka 1982, followed by Keiji Nishioka 1985 | **CONFIRMED MODULO THE UNVERIFIED KEIJI NISHIOKA 1985 STATEMENT** | Kumiko 1982 gives algebraicity of the critical product. The unverified 1985 implication is then needed to make that algebraic germ rational. |
| Corollary 5.3, binary linear sampling order | Keiji Nishioka 1985 through Theorem 5.1, after the Kumiko 1982 step | **CONFIRMED MODULO THE UNVERIFIED KEIJI NISHIOKA 1985 STATEMENT**, with the existing correction \(V\ge6\) | The lower bound is unconditional. Only the upper bound \(\mathsf N_{C_2}(V)\le V\), and hence the \(\Theta(V)\) conclusion, inherits `(KN85)`. |
| Theorem 6.1, odd-prime delayed multi-collisions | None | **CONFIRMED** | Explicit determinant, matrix, spectral-gap, profile-collision, and first-discrepancy calculations. |

None of the five results depends on Kumiko Nishioka 1982 alone. Theorem 5.1 is the only primary result that uses Kumiko 1982, and it subsequently requires the Keiji 1985 interface.

**Hypothesis Boundary**

For Theorem 2.1, the required hypotheses are \(p\ge2\), normalized reduced fractions
\[
H=\frac{P_0}{P_1}=\frac{R(z^p)}{R(z)^p},\qquad
P_0(0)=P_1(0)=R(0)=1,
\]
with \(P_0,P_1\in\mathbb Q[z]\), \(R\in\mathbb Q(z)^\times\), and \(D=\deg P_0+\deg P_1\). These are internal hypotheses; no external theorem is used.

Theorem 3.1 adds \(R\ne1\), positivity \(R(t)>0\) on the stated real interval, and the definitions
\[
\nu=\operatorname{ord}_0(R-1),\qquad
c_x(R)=\#\{y\in(0,x):R(y)=1\}.
\]
Again, all inputs are internal.

Theorem 5.1 requires:

- \(\ell\) prime and \(G\) a finite abelian \(\ell\)-group.
- Primitive nonnegative integral base matrices \(A,A'\), with the stated Perron interval.
- Relative unit-Adams invariance.
- Agreement of the first \(L\) primitive length-element vectors.
- \(K\) distinct interior profile collisions, one at an algebraic radius.
- The applicable threshold on \(K+L\).
- The explicitly quoted assumption `(KN85)`.

Everything except `(KN85)` and the published Kumiko special-value theorem is established internally. Corollary 5.3 inherits these hypotheses in the binary specialization and separately requires \(V\ge6\).

Theorem 6.1 assumes only an odd prime \(\ell\ge3\) and \(m\ge1\); its systems are constructed explicitly.

**The Descent Step**

The descent to the relative ratio \(H_\chi\) itself is valid:

- Relative unit-Adams invariance genuinely gives \(H_\chi\in\mathbb Q(z)\).
- Perron domination supplies the required zero- and pole-free disk.
- The algebraic sample lies inside that disk, so its full power orbit avoids zeros and poles.
- The coefficient-height and common-denominator estimates required by Kumiko Nishioka 1982 are established for this rational input.
- The checked Kumiko theorem therefore implies that
  \[
  F_\chi(z)=\prod_{j\ge0}H_\chi(z^{\ell^j})^{\ell^{-j}}
  \]
  is algebraic over \(\mathbb C(z)\).

That is exactly where the proof stops using verified inputs. Kumiko 1982 alone does not produce \(F_\chi\in\mathbb C(z)\), so it does not produce the rational certificate \(R_\chi=F_\chi^{-1}\). Without that certificate, the squarefree collision-jet inequality cannot be applied and character induction does not close.

The exact Keiji 1985 statement required to close the proof mechanically is now quoted in the theorem hypothesis:

> For every integer \(p\ge2\) and every \(H\in\mathbb C(z)^\times\), every convergent Laurent-series germ \(F\in\mathbb C((z))\) that is algebraic over \(\mathbb C(z)\) and satisfies
> \[
> F(z^p)=\frac{F(z)^p}{H(z)}
> \]
> belongs to \(\mathbb C(z)\).

Once this implication is verified from the original paper, the remaining descent is elementary: rational Taylor coefficients give \(F\in\mathbb Q(z)\) by coefficientwise Galois invariance, and \(R=F^{-1}\) gives
\[
H(z)=\frac{R(z^p)}{R(z)^p}.
\]

The pre-certificate portion of Theorem 5.1 is salvageable with Kumiko 1982 alone: base-determinant recovery, the prime-primary Adams-Möbius collapse, rationality and zero-freedom of \(H_\chi\), the algebraic collision identity, and algebraicity of \(F_\chi\). The rigidity conclusion and linear upper bound are not.
